title: `torch.nn.functional.max_pool1/2/3d` and `torch.quantized_max_pool1/2d` can not handle several edge cases in 1.13.1

labels.name: module: error checking
labels.description: Bugs related to incorrect/lacking error checking

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug When the argument (e.g., `dilation`) input is a list, if its value is over the upper bound of int64, `torch.nn.functional.max_pool1/2/3d` and `torch.quantized_max_pool1/2d` will report TypeError instead of throwing an overflow error: ``` TypeError: max_pool1d(): argument 'dilation' must be tuple of ints, but found element of type int at pos 1 ``` In [#73840](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/73840), a similar problem on `torch.max_pool1d` was first reported and confirmed as an edge case to be fixed. However, similar bugs on `torch.nn.functional.max_pool` and `torch.quantized_max_pool` exist in 1.13.1 and other previous versions. In addition, there is another interesting behavior related to this bug. If the argument is not a list `[x]` but a direct value `x`, then there will raise an error for the overflow problem, which is expected behavior. ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "test.py", line 19, in test() File "test.py", line 18, in test func_cls(input, kernel_size=i , stride=i, padding=0, dilation=i, ceil_mode=True) RuntimeError: Overflow when unpacking long ``` ### To Reproduce ```python import torch import sys i = sys.maxsize + 1 func_cls=torch.quantized_max_pool2d # torch.nn.functional.max_pool1d # torch.nn.functional.max_pool2d # torch.nn.functional.max_pool3d # torch.quantized_max_pool1d # torch.quantized_max_pool2d input = torch.full((1, 32, 32,), 0.5) def test(): func_cls(input, kernel_size=[i] , stride=[i], padding=0, dilation=[i], ceil_mode=True) test() ``` ### Expected behavior For this type of edge case, an overflow error should be thrown (e.g., `RuntimeError: Overflow when unpacking long`) instead of raising a TypeError. ### Versions
